say: left side of her face is drooping
her husband says she was normal at 1:40
note: Unqualified droop: RACE facial 2, G.F.A.S.T. facial 1, and a deficit (§4, §4b, §4d). Only the LKW is the husband's.

say: right arm drifts down when he holds both arms out
note: Drift: G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 1, RACE arm 1, deficit. Eliquis -> apixaban, anticoagulant before meds.list (§5b); ASR often writes 'eloquis'.
Plavix (clopidogrel) is an antiplatelet: meds.list only, never meds.anticoagulant (§5a). Slurred = G.F.A.S.T. speech 1, no RACE aphasia (§5a).

say: woke up this morning with it, nobody saw it start
his wife says he was fine when he went to bed at 10 last night
note: Woke up with it = not witnessed; the wake-up is a discovery, no time. LKW is the bedtime, 'last night' adds pm (§4c, §5b). Coumadin -> warfarin.

say: eyes are deviated to the left
note: Gaze deviation: G.F.A.S.T. and RACE gaze 1. 'Can't speak' = RACE aphasia 2 and G.F.A.S.T. speech 1 (§4, §4d). Both positive findings are deficits (§4b).

say: she keeps using the wrong words
her daughter says she was last normal at 0630
note: Wrong words = language trouble with no severity: G.F.A.S.T. speech 1 and a deficit, no RACE value (§5b). A negative face gives only the 0s (§4b). 0630 is 24-hour.
RACE item scores give the RACE items and the derived G.F.A.S.T. items, but no deficits (§4d, §5b). The son saw it: family, labeled because the dispatch is a stroke (§4c, §5b).

say: her husband says she doesn't take any blood thinners
note: 'GFAST positive, all four' = all four items 1, no deficits (§4d, §5b). 'This morning' adds am. The husband's explicit denial -> 'none', family.

say: crushing chest pain that started 40 minutes ago
we gave aspirin 324 milligrams by mouth
note: A 12-lead 'done at' gives the time, not ecg.attached (§5b). Aspirin by the crew is meds.given, not meds.list (§4b, §4e); 'by mouth' = PO.

say: 12-lead is attached, no STEMI on it
she tells me she's allergic to penicillin
note: Onset keeps 'since', 'this morning' adds am (§5b). 'No STEMI' -> stemi_reading false (§4e). 'She tells me' makes the allergy the patient's (§3).

say: took one of his own nitro pills before we got there
12-lead has been transmitted to the hospital
note: His own nitro before EMS arrived is a home med (meds.list), not meds.given (§4b, §4e). No hospital is named, so no destination.

say: we gave nitro 0.4 milligrams under the tongue, two doses
note: Two doses said as a count = one meds.given fact with count 2 (§4e); 'under the tongue' = SL. 'No known allergies' -> [] (medic shorthand, §5b).

say: tripped on the rug and fell
facts: tripped on the rug and fell
note: The fall is both the complaint and the mechanism (§4, §4e). No height and no head strike: no trauma.criteria; the anticoagulant is never a trauma.criteria value (§4e).

say: driver wasn't wearing a seatbelt and was thrown from the car
facts: rollover, unrestrained driver, thrown from the car
note: Rollover with no seatbelt = 'rollover unrestrained'; thrown from the car = 'ejection' (§4e). Components only: never compute a GCS total (§4e).

say: stab wound to the upper left thigh
we put a tourniquet on the left thigh at 22:10
facts: penetrating injury head neck torso or proximal extremity
bleeding requiring tourniquet or wound packing
note: A penetrating wound gives complaint, mechanism and injury (§4e). Thigh = proximal extremity; the tourniquet gives the bleeding criterion (§4e).

say: fell about 12 feet off a roof
obvious deformity of the right wrist
note: 'About' is an approximator, not a hedge, so the height counts (§4e). One deformed wrist is an injury, not a trauma criterion.

say: pedestrian hit by a car and thrown about 20 feet
facts: pedestrian hit by a car, thrown 20 feet
pedestrian or cyclist thrown or run over
note: An unstable pelvis is an injury and the 'pelvic fracture' criterion (§4e). Only the systolic is on the card; the GCS is a total, no parts.

say: the nursing home nurse says she's being treated for a urinary tract infection
note: Nursing-home staff count as family (§3, §5b). 102.4 F -> 39.1 C (§4).

say: he's confused, which is new for him
note: New confusion -> ACVPU C, not a complaint (§4, §4c). 'Room air' -> on_oxygen false. 'Looks like pneumonia' -> respiratory (§4e).

say: red, swollen wound on his left foot that looks infected
note: 100.9 is Fahrenheit by magnitude -> 38.3 C (§4). The infected wound is infection 'skin', not a trauma injury, and not a complaint (§4c).

say: recheck sugar 124, now alert and oriented
note: A recheck is a second fact, not a correction (§4b, §4c). D10 -> dextrose (§4e). Hypoglycemia gets no stroke keys (§4c).

say: his roommate says he sprayed one dose of Narcan up his nose
fire gave another 4 milligrams of Narcan in the nose
note: Doses given before arrival by others are meds.given with 'by' as a category: roommate -> bystander, fire -> fire (§4e). Narcan -> naloxone.

say: her mom says she had a seizure at 3:10 that lasted about 2 minutes
note: A seizure isn't stroke-like: no stroke.* keys even though the mother saw it (§4c). Keppra -> levetiracetam (ASR often mangles it).

say: we gave albuterol 5 milligrams by neb
note: A drug given by the crew is meds.given, not meds.list (§4b). The allergy has no attribution, so it's the medic's.

speaker: wife
say: he was fine at 8:30 this morning
I watched his face droop while he was talking to me
note: Wife's mic: all family (§3, §5a). Her account of the droop is a deficit only, never G.F.A.S.T./RACE (§4d, §5b). Pradaxa -> dabigatran; both drug names are often misheard.

speaker: daughter
say: Mom fell getting out of bed
she has a POLST that says do not resuscitate
she takes warfarin and a water pill
note: 'A water pill' is a drug class with no name: no meds.list item (§4c). POLST DNR -> 'DNR' (§4).

speaker: patient
say: the pain in my chest started about an hour ago
note: Patient on the mic: role patient. Brilinta (ticagrelor) is an antiplatelet: no anticoagulant (§5a). 'About' is dropped from the time (§4c).

speaker: neighbor
say: I found her on the kitchen floor this morning
she was fine when I talked to her at 5 pm yesterday
her right arm is limp and she can't talk
note: Neighbor's mic: bystander (§3). No stroke dispatch, but stroke-like symptoms are described, so 'found' and the LKW are labeled (§4c). The discovery time gives nothing (§5b).

speaker: husband
say: she took her insulin this morning but skipped breakfast
her sugar on our meter was 41
I gave her a tube of glucose gel
note: Her own insulin dose is meds.list; the gel her husband gave is meds.given, by 'family' (§4e). Oral glucose gel -> 'glucose'.

speaker: son
say: he's not on any blood thinners anymore, he stopped his Xarelto last month
his neighbor told me he looked fine getting the mail at 7:45 this morning
he's full code, he wants everything done
note: Stopped Xarelto: no meds.list, but 'not on any blood thinners' is an explicit denial -> 'none' (§5b). The neighbor's LKW relayed by the son is bystander (§4b).
